traces.description: A network drop occurs after caps has already finished but auth is still pending. Reconnecting must resume exactly that partial atomic sub-configuration via the deep <history id=conn_history> -- NOT restart both regions from their default entry (which would incorrectly re-enter caps_pending). This is the case the design spike's Finding 4 identified as requiring a real stateful history tracker, not the default-entry algorithm used for reachability checks.

steps.note: first-ever visit: conn_history has nothing stored yet, so it resolves via its own default <transition target=negotiating>, which is default-entry (fans into both regions' initial sub-states).
on exiting the connecting/negotiating subtree, conn_history must record the exact pre-drop sub-configuration {auth_pending, caps_done}, not just that 'negotiating' was active.

re-entry must restore the RECORDED sub-configuration {auth_pending, caps_done}, not the chart's default entry configuration {auth_pending, caps_pending} -- a history-blind implementation would incorrectly restart caps from caps_pending here. This is the assertion this trace exists to make.
